findings.description: The 'every side is a known binary' rule only reads `path` at the merge-base and at the branch. For a rename, `gitDiffNumstat` reports only the new path, so the rename's source file is never checked or counted. Renaming a source file into a `.png` therefore drops all its deleted lines, with no forged flag.
findings.body:
**Renaming a source file into a known binary drops its deleted lines from the diff-size count**

The new rule skips a `-\t-` file only when every side it exists on is a known binary. For a rename, though, only the new path is ever checked. `gitDiffNumstat` pins `diff.renames=true` and keeps only the new path of a rename record:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/35168083e9a643db281ef06b8aebba81b6989412/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L729-L733

`gitDiffBinaryRecount` then runs `ls-tree` for that new path at the merge base. Nothing is listed, so the base side is `undefined`, and `spendKnownBinarySkip([undefined, n])` skips the file:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/35168083e9a643db281ef06b8aebba81b6989412/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L818-L824

**How to reach it:** a branch deletes `src/auth.ts` and adds `assets/a.png`. The PNG holds the PNG signature, a NUL, and at least half of `auth.ts`'s bytes. It is 1 MiB or less and contains no `PK\x05\x06`. git's rename detection does not exclude binary blobs, so it pairs the two files at 50% or more similarity, and numstat reports `-\t-` under `assets/a.png` only. Every line of `auth.ts` is deleted without being counted, and no forged flag is raised. The same deletion without the rename shows as `0\tN\tsrc/auth.ts` in numstat, and all N lines are counted.

If the budget is already spent, the file is recounted, but the recount loses the deletions too. `diffHunks` limits the diff to `:(top,literal)<new path>`, so git never sees the old path and reports a pure add.

The old rule ("either side binary") had the same hole, so this is not a regression. But this PR sets out to recount a text file that a known binary replaces (ADR 0154: "every side of the merge-base diff it exists on"), and a rename gets around that rule. The ADR's ceilings cover content inside a capped known binary. They do not cover a source file's deletions.

**Possible fixes:**
- Treat a rename source as a merge-base side. Carry the old path from numstat into `DiffFileStat`, run `blobIsKnownBinary(base, oldPath, …)` on it, and recount with both paths in the pathspec.
- Or run the numstat with `--no-renames`, so the deletion appears as its own entry and is counted.

A test would pin it: delete a multi-line `.ts` file and add a `.png` (signature + NUL + most of the `.ts` bytes), then assert that the diff-size count includes the deleted lines, or that the file is flagged.

findings.description: Test adequacy: no test fails if the new `--no-relative` in rawDiffEntries is removed. The new core.worktree + diff.relative test has no rename and no symlink with a test name, so an empty raw map changes no count.
findings.body:
**Test adequacy: nothing pins `--no-relative` in `rawDiffEntries`**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/35168083e9a643db281ef06b8aebba81b6989412/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L242-L243

```ts
      // A session-written `diff.relative` would list only a prefix's paths (decision 154).
      '--no-relative',
```

`diffSizeKind` gets a path's symlink mode (`entry?.mode === '120000'`) and its rename source (`entry?.renamedFrom`) only from the `--raw` listing. Suppose a session writes a `core.worktree` naming the repo's parent plus `diff.relative=true`. Without this flag, git then works under a `<repo>/` prefix that no tree path matches, and the raw map comes back empty.

The new test [`counts from the top of the tree under a core.worktree above the repo`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/35168083e9a643db281ef06b8aebba81b6989412/src/core/merge-gate.test.ts#L1673-L1694) still passes with line 243 deleted, because every fixture path gets the same kind without the raw map:
- `src/link.ts` is source by name.
- `src/other.test.ts` is source via `tree.linked`.
- `src/big.test.ts` is source via the grep reach.
- Every path is an addition, so there is no rename.

The test's `diff.relative` assertion only covers the numstat's `--no-relative`, which comes from `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS`.

**Mutant that survives:** under that config, a committed symlink `src/alias.test.ts` (mode `120000`) counts as test instead of source. So does a rename `src/impl.ts` → `src/impl.test.ts`. Either way, source lines move out of the source count and can stay under the diff-size flag.

**Fix:** add `['120000', 'src/alias.test.ts', 'imp.ts']` to that test's `commitBlobs` and expect `source: 17`. Without the flag it would count 16 source lines and 1 test line.

findings.description: readBlobs sets maxBuffer to the exact stdout size it expects, and leaves stderr piped into the same limit. So any git warning on stderr (for example a stale `.git/objects/info/alternates` entry) kills `cat-file --batch` with ENOBUFS, and every known-binary check and batched reach read then fails closed with an error that hides the cause. Add slack to maxBuffer or set stdio to ['pipe','pipe','ignore'].

The blobIsKnownBinary docstring says only an empty ls-tree listing answers undefined, but the code also answers undefined when the listing is non-empty and no record's path matches exactly. Nothing reaches this today under --full-tree -z. Either make the docstring true or return false/throw on a non-matching listing.

The ADR says the recount runs `merge-base` and one `diff` per `-\t-` file (two processes each). A known-extension file now also costs up to two `ls-tree` calls and a `cat-file --batch` read, so the stated per-file cost is too low for anyone sizing the batching follow-up.

The re-export of BINARY_FREE_MAX_BYTES/BINARY_FREE_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES from git-diff.client.ts exists only so merge-gate.service.ts can import the caps through the client. Importing them from ./known-binary.utils.js directly removes the re-export and its doc comment.

docs/conventions/testing.md §Layout asks for one test file per source file, but the new known-binary.utils.ts helpers are tested inside git-diff-client.test.ts. Sibling *.utils.ts modules each have their own *-utils.test.ts.

In readBlobs, the inline comment about `ls-tree -l` listing `BAD` repeats the JSDoc sentence just above it (and mayBeKnownBinary's JSDoc says it a third time). AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete the call-site copy.

The BinaryFormat type passes through gitDiffBinaryRecount, blobIsKnownBinary and knownBinarySize only so its magic can be tested. formatsNamed could return a flat string[] of magics, which removes the exported type and the destructuring in opensWithMagic.

The blobIsKnownBinary and gitDiffBinaryRecount JSDoc re-list the full skip criteria (and name internal helpers) that known-binary.utils.ts and ADR 0154 already state, so a change to the criteria must be made in three places. Keep the contract and point to knownBinarySize.

Swapping the global --literal-pathspecs for `:(top,literal)` magic means an inherited GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 (which scrubbedGitEnv does not strip) makes diffHunks match nothing and recount a forged file as 0 lines. Only the operator's environment can set it. Consider adding the GIT_*_PATHSPECS variables to the scrubbed list.
